hypothesis: An automated model drift and routing RCA component, integrated with canary/shadow routing and LLM quality evaluators, will (a) detect a bad model rollout (drift and/or routing misconfiguration) within 5 minutes, and (b) correctly attribute at least 90% of detected regressions to the true root cause (model vs. routing vs. upstream/downstream change), while maintaining <5% false-positive rollback recommendations compared to a baseline of metrics-only monitoring without RCA.

baseline.description: Production-like LLM gateway with multi-model routing using canary releases, but without specialized model drift detection or automated routing RCA. Engineers rely on generic infrastructure metrics (latency, error rate, CPU), token usage, and coarse business metrics displayed in dashboards (e.g., Grafana). No explicit experiment IDs, no per-model quality evaluation, and no automated attribution logic or rollback recommendations.
components: LLM Gateway Service (Python/FastAPI) exposing /chat and /admin endpoints
Static routing configuration mapping traffic percentages to model versions (e.g., model_v1 stable, model_v2 canary)
Simple load generator sending requests with randomly sampled tasks/intents
Metrics collection: latency (p50/p95), error rate, tokens per request, cost per request (estimated), exposed via Prometheus/OpenMetrics
Dashboards (Grafana or similar) displaying aggregate metrics by route but not attributing regressions to specific causes

detection_capabilities.quality_evaluation: None (no LLM-as-judge or rule-based quality metrics)
detection_capabilities.regression_alerts: Static threshold-based alerts on latency and error rate only, configured at gateway level rather than per-model/per-experiment

treatment.description: Same LLM gateway and routing setup as baseline, augmented with a model drift and routing RCA component that logs routing decisions, tracks per-model/per-experiment cohorts, runs automated quality evaluation on sampled requests, performs statistical regression detection on quality/latency/cost, and automatically attributes detected regressions to model-level drift, routing misconfiguration, or upstream/downstream changes. It emits structured RCA findings and (optionally) posts rollback recommendations via a remediation API.
components: LLM Gateway Service (same as baseline) extended to emit structured events with model_id, model_version, experiment_id, routing_decision, and traffic_mode (control/canary/shadow)
Routing Decision Logger and Audit Store (e.g., PostgreSQL or SQLite; alternatively, a file-based store for local runs)
Model Drift and Routing RCA Service implemented in Python, consuming structured events and metrics via a streaming interface (e.g., Kafka) or polling DB/files
Quality Evaluator: LLM-as-judge or deterministic heuristic evaluator for synthetic tasks, producing scalar quality scores per request
Experiment Manager providing canary, shadow, and A/B tagging and configuration via YAML in the repo
Regression Detector computing time-windowed statistics and change-point detection for quality, latency, and cost per request, stratified by model_id and experiment_id
Attribution Engine applying rules to separate regressions caused by new model versions, routing weight changes, and upstream/downstream changes (e.g., prompt template version changes or RAG toggles)
RCA Output Sink publishing RCA reports as JSON to a directory, database table, or HTTP endpoint, and optionally exposing a /recommendations endpoint for Chapter 12 integration

routing_behavior.strategy: Weighted random routing with experiment-aware labels

detection_capabilities.drift_detection: Statistical comparison of quality metrics and token usage distributions between stable and candidate models over sliding windows
detection_capabilities.quality_evaluation: LLM-as-judge or reference-based heuristic scoring on a labeled synthetic workload; evaluations stored with per-request metadata
detection_capabilities.regression_alerts: Automated, per-model/per-experiment alerts on quality, latency, and cost regressions using relative and absolute thresholds; alerts feed into RCA
detection_capabilities.root_cause_attribution: Rule-based attribution using change logs (model routing/version changes, config changes) and metric patterns to label regressions as model_drift, routing_misconfig, upstream_change, downstream_change, or mixed

workloads.name: synthetic_eval_workload
workloads.description: A fixed corpus of synthetic evaluation prompts with deterministic or reference outputs, partitioned into multiple intent/task classes (e.g., factual QA, summarization, classification). Used to measure per-model quality drift and compare stable vs. canary/shadow models.

request_pattern.distribution: Poisson arrivals approximated via batched requests in a loop
request_pattern.prompt_selection: Uniform random over the evaluation corpus with fixed seed for reproducibility

workloads.name: synthetic_prod_like_workload
workloads.description: Higher-volume, partially unlabeled workload mimicking production usage patterns, including variable prompt lengths, temperature settings, and tools disabled. Used primarily for latency and cost regression detection and for testing routing misconfiguration scenarios.

request_pattern.distribution: Bursty traffic (alternating low and high RPS phases)

workloads.name: shadow_traffic_replay_workload
workloads.description: Replay of previously captured anonymized or synthetic request/response logs sent as shadow traffic to a candidate model route, ensuring identical inputs for control and treatment models. Used to test shadow routing decisions and quality drift under real-request distributions.

request_pattern.distribution: Trace-driven replay preserving original inter-arrival gaps (scaled by factor if needed)

environmental_controls.hardware: Fixed VM or container resources (e.g., 4 vCPUs, 16 GB RAM) for gateway and RCA services; stable GPU/LLM backend configuration if using hosted models
environmental_controls.network: Stable network conditions; if using external LLM APIs, limit experiments to off-peak hours or use recorded responses to avoid confounding variability
environmental_controls.concurrent_processes: No other heavy workloads on the same host during experiments
environmental_controls.time_sync: All services use synchronized clocks (e.g., NTP) for accurate time-windowing

configuration_controls.prompt_templates: Fixed prompt templates across baseline and treatment; any changes logged via a config change log to distinguish upstream/downstream changes

model_backends.control_model: model_v1_stable (e.g., local LLM or specific vendor model/version)
model_backends.canary_model_bad: model_v3_candidate_bad (simulated drift or regression via wrapper or parameter changes)

configuration_controls.evaluation_config: Same evaluator model and evaluation rubric between baseline and treatment where applicable; baseline may not use evaluator outputs for RCA but can log them for offline comparison

phases: Phase 0: Warm-up (10 minutes) with only control model_v1_stable receiving 100% traffic
Phase 1: Good canary rollout (model_v2_candidate_good at 10–20% traffic) with no intentional regressions
Phase 2: Bad canary rollout (model_v3_candidate_bad at 10–20% traffic) inducing quality and/or latency/cost regressions
Phase 3: Routing misconfiguration scenario (e.g., inverted weights or stale config that sends high-value traffic disproportionately to canary)
Phase 4: Upstream/downstream change scenario (e.g., prompt template change or RAG toggle) without changing models, to test attribution specificity

baseline_vs_treatment_runs.baseline_run: Gateway + workloads + generic metrics only (RCA components disabled)
baseline_vs_treatment_runs.treatment_run: Gateway + workloads + full RCA stack enabled
baseline_vs_treatment_runs.order: Randomized or alternated to mitigate temporal drift (e.g., treatment then baseline, or baseline then treatment, documented in run logs)

metrics.name: quality_score
metrics.description: Evaluator-assigned quality score per request, averaged over sliding windows and grouped by model_id, model_version, and experiment_id.

metrics.name: quality_regression_delta
metrics.description: Difference in mean quality_score between canary/shadow model and stable control within a time window.

metrics.name: latency_p50
metrics.description: Median end-to-end request latency per model/experiment.

metrics.name: latency_p95
metrics.description: 95th percentile end-to-end request latency per model/experiment.

metrics.name: cost_per_request
metrics.description: Estimated cost per request based on tokens generated and vendor pricing or simulated pricing.

metrics.name: tokens_output
metrics.description: Number of output tokens per response, used for cost and drift analysis.

metrics.name: drift_detection_time
metrics.description: Time elapsed between the start of a bad rollout (or misconfiguration) and the first correct regression detection event by the RCA component.

metrics.name: attribution_accuracy
metrics.description: Fraction of detected regression episodes for which the RCA component correctly labels the primary root cause (model_drift, routing_misconfig, upstream_change, downstream_change) compared to a ground-truth incident script.

metrics.name: false_positive_rate_rollbacks
metrics.description: Fraction of RCA-generated rollback recommendations that correspond to scenarios where no material regression (above pre-defined thresholds) is present.

metrics.name: false_negative_rate_regressions
metrics.description: Fraction of simulated bad rollout scenarios where a regression is present but not detected above threshold by the RCA system within the observation window.

metrics.name: time_to_first_alert
metrics.description: Time from the onset of a bad rollout or misconfiguration to the first emitted alert or RCA report; measured for both baseline (if any generic alerts) and treatment.

metrics.name: rca_processing_overhead
metrics.description: Additional per-request processing time introduced by RCA instrumentation (event logging, evaluation sampling) compared to baseline.

primary.name: drift_detection_time
primary.target: <= 300 seconds for bad canary rollout scenarios
primary.interpretation: The RCA system should detect quality or latency/cost regressions from a bad canary within 5 minutes under the specified workloads.

primary.name: attribution_accuracy
primary.interpretation: At least 90% of regression episodes are correctly attributed to the scripted root cause category across all experimental phases.

secondary.name: false_positive_rate_rollbacks
secondary.interpretation: Fewer than 5% of rollback recommendations are issued in scenarios where regressions do not exceed defined thresholds.

secondary.name: false_negative_rate_regressions
secondary.interpretation: The RCA system fails to detect no more than 10% of scripted regression episodes within the observation window.

secondary.name: rca_processing_overhead
secondary.interpretation: Additional overhead introduced by RCA instrumentation remains operationally acceptable for typical enterprise LLM gateways.

comparison_with_baseline.expected_improvement: >= 2x faster detection for model-related regressions in the treatment compared to baseline metrics-only alerts, where applicable.

comparison_with_baseline.baseline_expectation: Baseline has no structured attribution or performs manual attribution offline; thus, treatment should provide quantifiable attribution where baseline does not.

failure_modes.name: no_regression_detected
failure_modes.description: Bad rollback or routing misconfiguration scenarios do not trigger regression detection within the observation window.
potential_causes: Sampling rate for evaluation too low to capture significant signal.
Thresholds or statistical tests configured too conservatively.
Workload intensity insufficient to expose regressions.

failure_modes.name: misattributed_cause
failure_modes.description: RCA system detects a regression but attributes it to the wrong root cause class (e.g., routing_misconfig instead of model_drift).
potential_causes: Incomplete or misaligned change logs for model/routing/config changes.
Overlapping simultaneous changes (multiple causes within the same time window).
Heuristic rules that do not fully capture complex interactions between metrics.

failure_modes.name: excessive_false_positives
failure_modes.description: RCA system generates frequent regression alerts or rollback recommendations during stable or acceptable performance periods.
potential_causes: High natural variance in workload metrics not accounted for.
Insufficient warm-up period leading to unstable baselines.

failure_modes.name: high_rca_overhead
failure_modes.description: RCA instrumentation significantly increases request latency or resource usage, making it impractical for production.
potential_causes: Synchronous evaluation or logging in the request path.
Inefficient event serialization or database writes.
Excessively high sampling of expensive evaluators.

failure_modes.name: data_quality_issues
failure_modes.description: Missing or corrupted routing metadata, timestamps, or evaluation scores impede drift detection or attribution.
potential_causes: Backpressure or dropped messages in the ingestion pipeline.

software: FastAPI or similar web framework for the LLM Gateway Service
uvicorn or gunicorn for serving the gateway
Requests or httpx for load generation scripts
Pandas and NumPy for metrics aggregation and drift analysis
SciPy or a lightweight statistical testing library for significance tests (e.g., t-test, Mann-Whitney, KS test)
Optional: scikit-learn for additional drift metrics (e.g., KL divergence)
PostgreSQL or SQLite for routing and evaluation logs (SQLite recommended for local reproducibility)
Optional: Kafka or Redis Streams for streaming ingestion; otherwise, batch polling of DB/file is acceptable
Docker and Docker Compose (optional but recommended) to provide reproducible services
Prometheus and Grafana (optional) for baseline metrics dashboards

hardware.minimum: 4 vCPUs, 16 GB RAM on the main host or cluster for gateway, RCA service, and database. If using a local LLM, 1 GPU with 16 GB VRAM is recommended; if using external APIs, GPU is not required.
hardware.storage: At least 5 GB free disk space for logs, evaluation outputs, and metrics snapshots.

external_dependencies.llm_backend: Either (a) a local open-source LLM model served via an HTTP API, or (b) a vendor LLM API (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic). The same backend must be used across baseline and treatment.
external_dependencies.evaluator_model: An LLM used as a judge for evaluation (can be a smaller or cheaper model than the main serving model), or a deterministic reference-based scoring implementation.
external_dependencies.network: Outbound HTTPS access if vendor APIs are used; otherwise, local loopback for self-hosted models is sufficient.

run_instructions: 2. Set up a Python virtual environment and install dependencies:
* LLM backend type (local vs vendor API) and credentials if needed.
* Model identifiers for model_v1_stable, model_v2_candidate_good, model_v3_candidate_bad.
* Sampling rates for evaluation and RCA (e.g., evaluate 10% of requests).
* Phase schedule (start/end times or triggers) for each experimental phase.
4. Initialize the database and any required schemas:
5. Start the LLM Gateway Service (baseline/treatment use the same binary):
6. Start the Model Drift and Routing RCA Service (for treatment run only):
# In a new terminal with virtualenv activated
7. (Optional) Start Prometheus and Grafana for baseline dashboards using Docker Compose:
8. Generate the synthetic evaluation corpus (if not pre-generated):
9. Run the baseline experiment (no RCA service):
- Ensure ONLY the gateway service is running (stop the RCA service if running).
- Run the baseline driver script which orchestrates phases and workloads:
* Execute Phase 0–4 according to the schedule.
* Send traffic using synthetic_eval_workload and synthetic_prod_like_workload.
* Optionally log evaluator outputs for offline comparison.
* Record all metrics and events to the baseline output directory.
- Ensure both gateway and RCA services are running.
* Execute the same Phase 0–4 schedule as baseline with identical workloads (controlled via seeds).
* Tag each request with experiment_id and traffic_mode (control/canary/shadow).
* Trigger evaluator sampling and send events to the RCA service.
* Collect RCA outputs (regression detections, attributions, and recommendations).
11. (Optional) Run the shadow traffic replay workload in both baseline and treatment:
- Run the analysis script to compute metrics and generate comparison plots:
* drift_detection_time and time_to_first_alert for scripted bad rollouts.
- Verify that for each scripted bad rollout or misconfiguration scenario, the RCA report:
* Identifies the affected model(s) and routing changes.
* Attributes the regression to the expected root cause category.
- Commit experiment configuration and a summary of analysis outputs to a separate branch or directory (excluding secrets).
- Record environment details (software versions, LLM backend configuration) in a README within experiments/ch10_model_drift_routing/
15. To rerun with alternative thresholds or sampling settings:
- Use different run_ids in the output directory to keep runs separate (e.g., baseline_run1, treatment_run1, baseline_run2).

summary.description: High-level textual summary of the experiment run, environment, and whether primary/secondary success criteria were met.

fields.experiment_id: String identifier for the experiment (e.g., exp-model-drift-routing-rca-ch10).
fields.run_id: Unique string for this specific run (e.g., treatment_run1).
fields.date: ISO-8601 date/time when the experiment was executed.
fields.environment: Short description of environment (local, CI, staging, etc.).
fields.llm_backend: Backend used (local model name or vendor API version).
fields.notes: Free-text notes about anomalies, deviations from the plan, or configuration changes.

configuration_snapshot.description: Snapshot of the key configuration parameters used for the run.

fields.config_file_path: Path to the YAML config used.
fields.routing_weights_by_phase: Map of phase name to routing weights for each model.
fields.regression_thresholds: Quality/latency/cost thresholds used for regression detection.
fields.drift_detection_window: Time window size in seconds or number of requests for drift statistics.
fields.change_log: List of scripted changes (model version changes, routing misconfigurations, prompt/template toggles) with timestamps.

metrics_aggregate.description: Aggregated metrics across phases, models, and runs.

per_phase.num_requests: Integer number of requests in this cohort.

overall.drift_detection_time_seconds: Float or null if not detected.
overall.rca_processing_overhead_ms_per_request: Float difference between treatment and baseline.
overall.baseline_vs_treatment_alert_time_improve: Float representing speedup (baseline_time / treatment_time) if both exist.

rca_events.description: Detailed logs of RCA detections and attributions emitted during the treatment run.

events.event_id: Unique identifier for the RCA event.
events.incident_id: Logical incident or regression episode ID, used to group related events.
affected_models: List of model identifiers involved in the event.

metrics_snapshot.quality_score_delta: Float difference vs. control or historical baseline.
metrics_snapshot.latency_delta_ms: Float difference vs. control or baseline.
metrics_snapshot.cost_delta_usd: Float difference vs. control or baseline.

detected_regression_types: List of regression types (e.g., quality, latency, cost).
events.attributed_primary_cause: One of: model_drift, routing_misconfig, upstream_change, downstream_change, mixed, unknown.
events.cause_confidence: Float 0–1 representing confidence in the attribution.

recent_changes: List of change_log entries temporally correlated with the regression.
supporting_evidence.cohort_comparison: Structured summary comparing affected cohort vs. control cohorts.

statistical_test_results.test_name: Name of statistical test used (e.g., t_test, mann_whitney, ks_test).
statistical_test_results.effect_size: Float effect size or standardized mean difference.

recommended_actions: List of recommended actions (e.g., rollback_canary, adjust_routing_weights, revert_prompt_template, investigate_downstream_service).

raw_data_references.description: Pointers to raw log files, database tables, or trace IDs used in the analysis.

fields.gateway_logs_path: Path or URI to gateway logs for this run.
fields.evaluation_logs_path: Path or URI to evaluation outputs.
fields.routing_audit_log_path: Path or URI to routing decision logs.
fields.rca_reports_path: Path or URI to RCA JSON reports.
fields.metrics_export_path: Path or URI to Prometheus/OpenMetrics export or CSV/Parquet snapshots.
